name: Umurage platform learning library
notes: Built into the platform and available to every school for the levels it offers. Original activities aligned to the Rwanda competence-based curriculum; teachers confirm suitability before use.

items.subject: Mathematics
items.title: Multiplication as repeated addition
items.learningObjective: Represent multiplication with groups of equal objects and solve simple word problems.
teacherActivities: Draw four groups of three dots.
Write 4 × 3 as repeated addition.
Explain the answer using counters.
items.studentPractice: Four baskets contain three mangoes each. How many mangoes are there? Show two methods.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Kinyarwanda
items.title: Gusoma no kumva inkuru ngufi
items.learningObjective: Read a short age-appropriate story and identify the main character, setting and message.
teacherActivities: Read a teacher-approved short story.
Identify the main character and location.
Summarize the story in three sentences.
items.studentPractice: Andika interuro eshatu zivuga ibyo wumvise mu nkuru.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Mathematics
items.title: Fractions of a whole
items.learningObjective: Represent a fraction as equal parts and compare familiar unit fractions.
teacherActivities: Draw a rectangle and divide it into four equal parts.
Shade one quarter.
Compare one half and one quarter.
items.studentPractice: A family divides 12 oranges equally among 4 children. How many oranges does each child receive?

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: English
items.title: Reading comprehension: identifying main ideas
items.learningObjective: Read a short informational text and identify the main idea and supporting details.
teacherActivities: Read a short passage approved by the teacher.
Underline the main idea.
Write two facts from the passage.
items.studentPractice: Write four sentences summarizing an article about caring for the environment.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Science and Elementary Technology
items.title: Healthy habits and hygiene
items.learningObjective: Identify common everyday hygiene practices and explain why they help protect health.
teacherActivities: Identify handwashing moments in daily school life.
Demonstrate proper handwashing.
Create a class hygiene poster.
items.studentPractice: List five actions that help keep your classroom clean.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Mathematics
items.title: Decimals in everyday quantities
items.learningObjective: Read, compare and order simple decimal numbers in meaningful contexts.
teacherActivities: Write everyday measurements using decimals.
Explain the value of the tenths place.
items.studentPractice: Arrange 2.4 L, 2.04 L and 2.44 L from least to greatest.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Science and Elementary Technology
items.title: Simple electrical circuits
items.learningObjective: Recognize basic circuit components and distinguish open and closed circuits.
teacherActivities: Identify a cell, lamp, switch and wire.
Draw a safe low-voltage circuit diagram.
Explain why the lamp goes out when a circuit opens.
items.studentPractice: Draw and label a circuit with a switch and bulb. Do not use mains electricity.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Social and Religious Studies
items.title: Responsible care for our community
items.learningObjective: Describe ways citizens can protect shared resources and cooperate respectfully.
teacherActivities: List shared school facilities.
Discuss ways to prevent damage.
Plan a class clean-up activity.
items.studentPractice: Write three examples of taking responsibility for shared property.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Mathematics
items.title: Ratios in simple situations
items.learningObjective: Express and simplify ratios using whole-number examples.
teacherActivities: Count blue and green counters.
Write the ratio of blue to green counters.
Simplify a ratio such as 6:9.
items.studentPractice: In a group there are 12 notebooks and 18 pencils. Simplify the notebooks-to-pencils ratio.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: ICT
items.title: Researching reliable online resources
items.learningObjective: Recognize trustworthy online sources and protect personal information while learning.
teacherActivities: Compare official education websites and advertisements.
Identify author, date and institution on a web page.
Discuss why student passwords should stay private.
items.studentPractice: Find one REB resource with your teacher and record its title and topic without sharing your personal details.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: French
items.title: Se présenter et présenter son école
items.learningObjective: Use short French sentences to introduce oneself and describe one's school.
teacherActivities: Practice Je m'appelle…
Describe a classroom using common nouns.
Write three simple school-related sentences.
items.studentPractice: Écris cinq phrases courtes sur ton école fictive.

sources.label: REB Curriculum, Teaching and Learning Resources Department

items.subject: Language and communication
items.title: My name and my family
items.learningObjective: Say their own name and name two family members in a full sentence.
teacherActivities: Sit in a circle and model: My name is ... I live with ...
Pass a soft ball; each child says their name when they catch it.
Praise every full sentence and repeat it back.
items.studentPractice: At home, tell a family member the names of two friends from class.

items.subject: Language and communication
items.title: Story time with picture cards
items.learningObjective: Retell a short story in the right order using three picture cards.
teacherActivities: Tell a short story about a goat looking for water, showing one card per event.
Mix the cards and ask the class to put them back in order.
Ask: What happened first? Next? At the end?
items.studentPractice: Draw one picture from the story and tell a grown-up what happens.

items.subject: Numeracy and early mathematics
items.title: Counting beans to five
items.learningObjective: Count up to five objects and match the count to a number card.
teacherActivities: Give each child a cup with beans.
Call a number from 1 to 5; children count out that many beans.
Hold up the matching number card together.
items.studentPractice: Count spoons, cups or shoes at home and say the number out loud.

items.subject: Numeracy and early mathematics
items.title: Shapes around our classroom
items.learningObjective: Name circle, square and triangle and find each shape in the classroom.
teacherActivities: Show cut-out shapes and trace the edges with a finger.
Go on a shape hunt around the room in small groups.
Sort found objects into three shape baskets.
items.studentPractice: Find one circle, one square and one triangle at home.

items.subject: Social and emotional development
items.title: How do I feel today?
items.learningObjective: Name a feeling (happy, sad, angry, scared) and say why.
teacherActivities: Show four face cards and act out each feeling.
Each child points to a face and finishes: I feel ... because ...
Agree on one kind thing to do when a friend feels sad.
items.studentPractice: Tell a grown-up one feeling you had today and why.

items.subject: Social and emotional development
items.title: Taking turns and sharing
items.learningObjective: Wait for a turn and share materials in a small group game.
teacherActivities: Play a simple rolling-ball game in groups of four.
Use a talking stick: only the holder speaks.
Notice and praise good turn-taking out loud.
items.studentPractice: Play a game at home where everyone takes turns.

items.subject: Physical development and health
items.title: Washing our hands
items.learningObjective: Wash hands with soap and water in the right steps.
teacherActivities: Demonstrate the five steps: wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry.
Sing a short song for the rubbing step so it lasts long enough.
Every child practises at the tap with a helper.
items.studentPractice: Show a family member the five hand-washing steps before eating.

items.subject: Physical development and health
items.title: Jump, hop and balance
items.learningObjective: Jump with two feet, hop on one foot and balance for five seconds.
teacherActivities: Warm up with stretching and marching in place.
Set up a line of hoops for jumping and a line for hopping.
Count to five together while children balance.
items.studentPractice: Practise balancing on one foot while a grown-up counts to five.

items.subject: Creative arts and culture
items.title: Traditional song and clapping
items.learningObjective: Sing a short traditional song and clap a steady beat.
teacherActivities: Teach the song line by line, children echoing each line.
Add a steady clap, then try soft and loud clapping.
Perform for another class or for parents.
items.studentPractice: Sing the song at home and teach the clapping to someone.

items.subject: Creative arts and culture
items.title: Imigongo-style patterns
items.learningObjective: Make a repeating pattern inspired by Rwandan imigongo art.
teacherActivities: Show pictures of imigongo zigzag and diamond patterns.
Children repeat a two-colour pattern with paper strips.
Display the patterns and let children describe them.
items.studentPractice: Make a pattern at home using leaves, stones or bottle caps.

items.subject: Environment and science
items.title: Plants need water
items.learningObjective: Say what a plant needs to grow and water a class plant.
teacherActivities: Show two bean seedlings: one watered, one dry.
Ask the class what they notice after three days.
Make a watering rota so each child has a turn.
items.studentPractice: Help water a plant at home and say how it looks.

items.subject: Environment and science
items.title: Animals and their homes
items.learningObjective: Match five common animals to where they live.
teacherActivities: Show pictures of a cow, bird, fish, dog and bee.
Children place each animal on the matching home picture.
Talk about how we care for animals.
items.studentPractice: Name an animal you saw today and where it lives.
